evidence: Receiving online DO sensor: ~12.1 mg/L at t=45.8h collapsing to 3.60 at t=46.0h and 1.73 mg/L at t=51.8h, below the 2 mg/L limit
Source batches 1-3 remained at 8-10.5 mg/L DO over the same window, confirming a receiving-tank-specific fault
Forward model, all actions: post_decision_feasible=false; min DO 0.90 (increase_air), 0.88 (reduce_feed), 1.00 (combined), 1.18 (strong_feed_reduction), 1.25 (keep)
Sensitivity sets: 0/5 feasible members for every action, best sensitivity min DO 1.81 mg/L (strong_feed_reduction) — still below the 2 mg/L limit
Delayed product assay available at t=52h (sampled t=48h): 2.72 g/L, confirming on-line production continued under oxygen stress
args.rationale: The receiving tank suffered an abrupt oxygen-transfer failure at ~46h (estimated transfer multiplier 0.45 of nominal, onset ~44h per the model update): online DO fell from ~12 mg/L to ~3.5 mg/L within one sampling interval and has declined monotonically to ~1.73 mg/L at the latest reading — already below the 2 mg/L hard limit. The source batches show no such collapse, confirming this is a receiving-specific fault, not normal dynamics. I evaluated every bounded intervention with the source-calibrated forward model. All are centrally predicted infeasible: increase_air min DO 0.90 mg/L, reduce_feed 0.88, combined 1.00, strong_feed_reduction 1.18 (best), keep 1.25 — all below 2 mg/L at some remaining time, with 7.2–11.2 h below limit and zero feasible members in every 5-member sensitivity set (best member 1.81 mg/L, still infeasible). Per the decision priorities, no operating plan can be justified as meeting the post-decision DO >= 2 mg/L constraint — a centrally infeasible plan is not rescued by uncalibrated sensitivity members — so stop is the required decision. Product mass (114–186 kg predicted) never compensates for a predicted oxygen-constraint violation, and continued operation would breach the hard limit for multiple hours under every available plan. This is an evidence-supported stop based on infeasibility of all bounded interventions, not a tool failure; the stable normal observations earlier in the run do not change this, since the failure is recent and worsening.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; the true receiving-process oxygen-transfer capacity is hidden and could in principle be better than the model's estimate. However, the directly observed receiving DO trajectory (1.73 mg/L and falling at the decision time) independently corroborates infeasibility without any model: DO is already below the limit, every bounded action takes hours to propagate (assay/sensor clocks: 4h assay turnaround, 0.2h sensor steps), and the trend over the last ~6h is monotonically downward with no evidence of stabilization. The best modeled alternative (strong_feed_reduction) still leaves ~7.2 h below the limit. Residual uncertainty about the exact onset time or transfer multiplier does not change the sign of the conclusion. A stop yields zero counted production, so this sacrifices the predicted ~115-135 kg of product mass; that trade-off is mandated by the hard-constraint priority ordering.
